I am 58 years old, farming these 28.1 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read fertilizer bags and understand what the township extension people say at the village meetings, but honestly, most of what I know comes from doing it year after year and watching what works on my neighbors' fields. At 28 mu my place is bigger than a lot of households around here, so I have to think about efficiency. I hire machinery for the heavy work — a combine for wheat harvest, a rotary tiller and planter for maize — because me and my wife can't handle it all alone, and my son only comes back from Handan for the busiest days.

My backbone is the wheat-maize double crop on 20 mu. That land has to pay the bills. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu for wheat and 500 kg for maize. This year I'll plant the same improved wheat seed I buy from the township supply store — about 12.5 kg per mu, costs 35 yuan per mu. For maize I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or something similar from the dealer, about 2.5 kg per mu at 50 yuan. I don't save maize seed — hybrids don't work the second year.

For wheat, after the maize comes off in early October, I plough deep and let the soil sit a few days. Before planting, I spread one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, costs 160 yuan a bag now, up from last year. Then at jointing in March, I topdress with another 15 kg of urea per mu. The extension agent said 12 kg is enough, but I put 15 kg because I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than see my wheat turn yellow and lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate four times: the freezing water before winter, jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling water. Pumping from my well costs electricity — about 25 yuan per mu each time — so it adds up, but you can't skip water on wheat.

Summer maize is the hard part because the window is so tight. Sometimes I only have five or six days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire the custom rotary tiller to go over the field fast — 40 yuan per mu — then the planter puts in seed and fertilizer together. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer and 15 kg of urea per mu all at once at planting. No time for split dressing with double cropping. I irrigate twice if the weather is dry: right after planting to get germination, and once at the big trumpet stage in July or August. If the rainy season is good, maybe only once.

I keep 4 mu in cotton. Cotton brings good cash when prices hold, but it needs more sprays and labor. I plough in April, put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress twice with 10 kg urea each time. Cotton needs three pesticide sprays minimum — herbicide at planting, then insecticide for bollworm. I used to pick it all by hand with family, but now I hire some picking labor because 4 mu is too much for us alone. I target about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

On the east side I put 1.5 mu in soybean. It's a legume so it doesn't need much nitrogen — just 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, one irrigation, one spray for weeds. Should get about 150 kg per mu. Mungbean gets 1 mu — quick crop, 60-70 days. I put 15 kg compound per mu, irrigate once, spray once. Expect about 100 kg per mu.

My wife grows spinach on 0.6 mu near the house — for eating and selling a bit at the county market. That small plot gets more attention: 30 kg compound and 10 kg urea per mu, two irrigations, two sprays. Spinach grows fast and yields heavy — about 1,200 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

I also plant 1 mu of chrysanthemum for the medicine buyer. I plough in April, put down 35 kg compound and 10 kg urea per mu. Two irrigations, two pesticide sprays. Hope to get 160 kg of dried flowers per mu.

The problem is always cash. Fertilizer prices went up again. Just for the wheat-maize on 20 mu, I'm spending over 4,000 yuan on fertilizer, plus seed, plus diesel, plus pump electricity, plus hiring the combine and planter. At my size I can absorb some risk, but I still hate waste. Last year I thought about cutting cotton to save labor, but cotton paid better than expected. So I keep it. The mungbean, soybean, spinach, and chrysanthemum spread my risk — if the weather goes bad on one crop, at least I didn't spend much on the small ones, and they bring cash at different times. One thing I learned the hard way: ten years ago I tried saving 200 yuan by using less compound fertilizer on wheat, and the crop came up yellow and thin. Lost almost 100 kg per mu. That mistake cost me ten times what I saved. Never again.
